scope: PAC-007 bounded review across eight product domains, not product certification or repair

domains.boundary: 26 sanitation cases pass; real PNG audit and date-only ZIP controls pass. Organizer retry/idempotence is defective. No hostile filesystem-race or forensic-erasure claim is established.

domains.evidence: Plan, model setup, task commit, status, review, resume checks, serving and pack source; synthetic exact-byte review/ZIP probe
domains.boundary: Candidate corruption is blocked at serving/packing. Status and rejection have the separate defect above. No real-model publishing run occurred.

Source distinguishes proxy metrics from effectiveness. Optional pre-commit probing is incomplete; old optimizer zero-gradient behavior remains a runtime hypothesis. No pretrained/CUDA/MPS/full-video result was produced.

domains.evidence: Server and JS flows; existing server tests; authenticated ASGI requests; isolated JS callback
domains.boundary: Homepage, body bound, job state and audit badge defects reproduced. Full DOM/browser, real TCP listener and external origin environments were not rerun.

domains.evidence: CLI/service/controller, operation lifecycle, keyboard/line input and relevant tests
domains.boundary: 120 terminal-core and 49 revision cases pass; line-form focus fails. Native Windows console, desktop viewer and actual POSIX terminal behavior were not tested in this audit.

domains.evidence: `pyproject.toml`, launchers, offline sdist-to-wheel build, isolated target install, imports and byte comparison
domains.boundary: All 47 application files agree in source, sdist, wheel and installed target. Dependencies were reused from `.venv`; clean-machine bootstrap and Python 3.11 compatibility were not established.

domains.evidence: Current full suite, test substitutions, old test logs, package equality manifest, browser QA scripts
domains.boundary: Historical logs contain 667-pass source/wheel results, with synthetic/native limitations documented. Ten historical package hashes differ from current files; those old results do not validate this checkout. Test counts are not feature coverage.

domains.evidence: `DEVELOPMENT-SPEC`, `WAVE-03-HANDOFF`, `WAVE-04`, `VALIDATION`, current PACER registers and prior completion audit
domains.boundary: Native/pretrained qualification, artist judgments, actual platform derivatives and modern text-conditioned/video efficacy remain pending or partial in the documents themselves. Narrow completed tasks cannot establish the whole roadmap is complete. PAC-015 retains the missing qualification scope.

findings.finding: A dated PNG has different `st_ctime_ns` through `fstat` and `Path.stat`. Organization reports `SOURCE_CHANGED_OUTPUT_RETAINED`; three retries leave the source and create three catalog entries. A newly saved, unmodified control completes. This is conditional, not a claim that every import fails.

findings.priority_and_evidence: High; real ASGI request and existing failing test
findings.finding: Browser `/` returns HTTP 500 on this Windows environment. UTF-8 HTML is read using cp1252; byte 0x81 raises `UnicodeDecodeError`.

An organization job with an unsupported text file returns `checkpoint: INCOMPLETE`, but the enclosing job says `state: done`, `phase: Complete`. Terminal workers correctly classify incomplete results as needing attention.

findings.priority_and_evidence: High; exact JS function executed with substituted DOM collaborators
findings.finding: Publishing completion unconditionally replaces the workspace audit with `checkpoint: COMPLETE`. A preexisting incomplete audit becomes complete even for a blocked batch, without another audit call. This is an isolated function reproduction, not a live browser session.

findings.priority_and_evidence: Medium; real review/status/export functions, synthetic committed records
findings.finding: After approving a valid candidate and changing its bytes, status still reports `READY_FOR_REVIEW / ACCEPTED`. Rejecting it fails with `PUBLICATION_ARTIFACT_CHANGED`, leaving the acceptance receipt. Serving and ZIP export correctly reject the changed artifact; this is stale status and blocked revocation, not an export bypass.

The same 40,015-byte JSON request is rejected with 413 when Content-Length is present but accepted with 200 when sent chunked. The advertised 32 KiB check only inspects the header. Authentication remains enforced; this is not an unauthenticated remote exploit demonstration.
`focus 3` in a six-field doctor form leaves cursor at field 1. `focus` counts page rows, while forms use a separate field list. The `down` control reaches field 2.

findings.priority_and_evidence: Medium; source plus controlled call-order instrumentation
findings.finding: The publishing contract says models pass a numerical input-gradient probe before request commit. Only encoders are probed. Optional inpainting and temporal adapters are instantiated but not executed before `request.json` is written. Instrumented deliberately non-executable optional adapters reach that commit boundary. This does not test real model numerics.

findings.priority_and_evidence: Low; live API read plus source
findings.finding: The installed package is 0.5.0, while `/api/state` reports 0.3.0. Generation reports also hardcode `application_version: 0.2.0` (source inspection only). Version evidence can therefore identify the wrong application release.

Three independent test assumptions fail on Windows: a fake stat object lacks `st_ctime`; migration snapshots use backslashes while the assertion replaces slashes; a symlink test assumes creation privileges. Eight entire modules skip at collection without Torch, including publication/API tests. Passing the remaining suite cannot certify those paths.

Legacy `optimizer.protect`, reachable through the encoder engine, starts with random noise, accepts finite zero gradients and returns without a positive-objective check. A differentiable constant encoder appears able to return random-start pixels. The production release guard has stronger checks. Torch is unavailable here, so this hypothesis requires a real-autograd reproduction before being called runtime-confirmed.
